learn.canDo: Explain a container as a restricted process, and choose the namespace, cgroup and hardening switches that contain it.
learn.why: 'Is a container a VM?' is a standard question. Knowing which switch controls which risk is the better answer.
learn.keyIdea: Seeing and using are different switches.

learn.canDo: Explain why layers only add, and cut an image's size and attack surface with multi-stage builds, same-layer cleanup and a small base.
learn.why: Image size is scale-up latency and attack surface. Reviewers look at Dockerfiles for exactly these habits.

learn.canDo: Order a Dockerfile for the build cache, keep the cache on CI, and use cache mounts for packages.
learn.why: Slow builds cost a team hours a day. Knowing why the cache breaks is a quick, visible win.

learn.canDo: Explain what survives a restart, a recreation and a host loss, and place data accordingly with backups.
learn.why: Losing data on a redeploy is the classic container mistake. Choosing storage by lifetime is the fix.

learn.canDo: Explain per-container localhost, connect services by name on a user-defined network, and publish only what outsiders need.
learn.why: 'Why can't my container connect to the database?' is the most common Docker question.
learn.keyIdea: Localhost is a namespace, not the machine.

learn.canDo: Explain why start order is not readiness, and make a Compose stack start reliably with healthchecks and resilient clients.
learn.why: Compose is the first orchestration tool most developers use. The readiness trap is its most common bug.

learn.canDo: Describe declared state and reconciliation, tune rolling updates, and spread replicas across failure domains.
learn.why: Kubernetes questions test whether you understand what the system guarantees and what it does not.

learn.canDo: Set memory limits from measured peaks, delay liveness past boot time, gate traffic with readiness, and size autoscaling for the spike.
learn.why: CrashLoopBackOff and slow scaling are the two production Kubernetes problems everyone meets.
learn.keyIdea: A limit is a kill switch with a number on it.

chapter.story: The team moves its services into containers and meets everything containers do not do for them.
outcomes: Explain what a container is and is not
Build small images and fast builds
Run on Kubernetes with probes, limits and autoscaling
chapter.why: Containers and Kubernetes are the default way to ship software. Most of their problems come from assuming they do more than they do.
chapter.payoff: In an interview you can explain containers and an orchestrator from first principles. At work you will review a Dockerfile and a manifest for the mistakes that cause outages.
